label: second original token when the first token is s
explanation: Fires only at step t=1, the second original input, in sequences whose first token is s, whatever the second token is. On dev the predicate matches exactly (P=R=F1=1.0, corr 0.999). Magnitude is nearly constant (0.52-0.58, i.e. 0.90-1.00 of max) and depends a little on the current input token: it is highest for o and lowest for d, v and n. It never fires at t=0 (on the s itself), at any later original step, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase, including when s is echoed back. It also never fires at t=1 when the first token is anything other than s.

issues: No refutation found. On the test split the predicate gets P=R=F1=1.0, mass recall 1.0 and correlation 0.9995 (16670 active, 16670 predicted). Misses on test show 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

The dev profile backs every structural claim. All firing is at t=1 / orig_idx=1 and all of it needs prev_tok=s (rate 0.091 at t=1 with first token s, which is 1/11 of steps where the previous token is s). It is 0 at t=0, at t>=2, on the delimiter and throughout the copy phase (copy phase 0 of 2.7M steps, including where s is echoed back).

The magnitude claim holds. Mean 0.550, max 0.584, and the low quartile is about 0.90 of max. The top examples are all s [o:1.00], and the lowest-quartile examples have d, v or n as the second token (0.90-0.91). The firing rate is flat across the current input token and across L, so nothing depends on token identity or length.

One minor point: under the predicate the feature also fires at t=1 when the second token is s (in_tok s, 618 steps). That fits 'whatever the second token is'. The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
